cost.label: Cost of living
cost.means: What a decent two-room flat costs each month in a neighbourhood where newcomers settle, plus everyday spending. The higher the score, the cheaper it is.
cost.doesNotMean: What locals pay, nor the cost of setting up.

rubric.1: A two-room flat costs over €900 a month, or everyday life costs almost as much as in Europe.
rubric.3: A two-room flat costs between €300 and €600.
rubric.5: A two-room flat costs under €200, on a market open to newcomers.

setupCost.label: Cost of settling in
setupCost.means: The money you pay out before the first month: rent in advance, deposit, agency fees, and the equipment the city makes necessary (a generator, a water tank).

rubric.1: A year's rent in advance or more, or over €5,000 before you move in.
rubric.3: Three to six months in all (deposit, advance, fees).
rubric.5: One month's rent with a deposit of one or two months.

negotiation.label: Room to haggle
negotiation.means: How far the asking price is only a starting point, for rent, taxis and the market.
negotiation.doesNotMean: That the city is expensive or dishonest: some people enjoy haggling, others do not.

rubric.1: Prices are mostly fixed: rents are kept to, taxis run on a meter or an app.
rubric.3: Rents and markets are commonly haggled over; shops and apps have fixed prices.
rubric.5: Almost every price is a starting point, rent and transport included.

safety.label: Everyday safety
safety.means: The risk of theft, assault or harassment for a careful resident, in the neighbourhoods where newcomers settle.
safety.doesNotMean: War or terrorism: a city in an area travel advice warns against is never suggested.

rubric.1: Travel advice names the city for armed robbery or kidnapping, or there is a curfew.
rubric.3: Theft and assault in some neighbourhoods, the usual care of any big city.
rubric.5: No particular risk reported; you can walk in the evening in most neighbourhoods.

utilities.label: Power and water
utilities.means: How often the power and water go off, and what it takes to cope.
utilities.doesNotMean: Access to the network: you can be connected and still have cuts.

rubric.1: Several hours of cuts almost every day; a generator and a water tank are essential.
rubric.3: Cuts every week or in some seasons; a backup is wise.
rubric.5: Rare, short cuts; no backup needed.

internet.label: Internet
internet.means: Can you work online from home?
internet.doesNotMean: Mobile coverage across the whole country.

rubric.3: 15 to 40 Mbit/s, fibre in some neighbourhoods.
rubric.5: Over 80 Mbit/s, fibre sold everywhere by several providers. A recent nationwide shutdown caps the score at 3.

healthcare.label: Healthcare
healthcare.means: The care you can get without leaving the country.
healthcare.doesNotMean: Public health across the whole country.

rubric.3: Private clinics for the basics; specialists or surgery in the capital.
rubric.5: An accredited hospital in the city and most specialities.

schools.label: Schools
schools.means: Places at a school following a curriculum a child can carry on elsewhere (French, English or international).
schools.doesNotMean: The quality of the local state school.

rubric.1: A small, partly recognised school, or distance learning only.
rubric.3: One recognised French or English school.
rubric.5: Several schools, in French and in English, up to the baccalauréat or its equivalent.

jobs.label: Jobs
jobs.means: Your chances of finding a skilled job locally when you arrive.

rubric.1: Almost no skilled jobs open to newcomers.
rubric.3: One or two sectors are hiring (the port, mining, government, tourism).
rubric.5: A regional hub hiring in every sector.

business.label: Starting a business and investing
business.means: How easy it is to start a business or invest.
business.doesNotMean: That a project is sure to succeed.

rubric.1: No incubator, no ranking, restricted ownership.
rubric.5: A hub known across the continent.

flights.label: Flights to Europe
flights.means: How easy it is to come and go.

rubric.1: No international airport within three hours.
rubric.3: One to three European cities by direct flight, within 1 h 30 of the city.
rubric.5: Eight or more European cities by direct flight.

culture.label: Cultural life
culture.means: Venues, festivals, museums, an arts scene.
culture.doesNotMean: How rich the people's own culture is, which is not something to score.

rubric.3: Venues and at least one festival known across the country.
rubric.5: A scene known across the continent, all year round.

nightlife.label: Going out
nightlife.means: What happens in the evening: bars, concerts, clubs.
nightlife.doesNotMean: A good or a bad mark: it is compared with your ideal Saturday night.

rubric.1: Alcohol banned, or almost nothing open after dinner.
rubric.3: A few bars and concerts at the weekend.
rubric.5: Every night, with a name across the region.

history.label: History and memory
history.means: The history you can visit, including places tied to the slave trade and the diaspora.
history.doesNotMean: The historical importance of a people.

rubric.3: One listed site or a major museum.
rubric.5: A World Heritage site in the city and memorial places of the diaspora.

returnees.label: Returnee network
returnees.means: An active network of people who have come back or come to settle, which a newcomer can join.
returnees.doesNotMean: How returnees are welcomed, which is not something to score.

rubric.5: A well-known place to return to, with regular meet-ups and a public desk for the diaspora.

pace.label: Pace of the city
pace.means: Traffic, crowds, noise, the speed of everyday life.
pace.doesNotMean: A good or a bad mark: it is compared with the city you are looking for.

rubric.1: A small town, little traffic, quiet evenings.
rubric.5: A megacity: traffic jams, crowds and noise day and night.
